; Per-issue regression corpus per SPECIFICATION.md §8.2. Every
; closed bug from the source-grammar projects gets one pinned
; S-expression here so a future grammar edit that breaks the
; closure surfaces as a single localised test failure.
;
; Cross-reference notes:
; - The murtaza64 #5 (juxt_function_call) anchor is pending: it
;   requires command-chain support which is not yet implemented.

================================================================================
Qualified commands, named arguments and statement boundaries
================================================================================

class Dsl {
  private final Number value
  private final Number epsilon
  Dsl(Number value, Number epsilon) { this.value = value; this.epsilon = epsilon }
  def run(client) {
    def data = client.decode 'text', String
    client.configure mode: 'test', count: 2
    def action = { target = 1 }
    [1, *[2, 3]].each { value -> client.send value, data }
    def values = new Object[2]
    def (String name, int count) = ['a', 2]
    assert count == 2, 'count'
  }
}

================================================================================
Closure defaults, annotation defaults, typed loops and casts
================================================================================

@interface Flag { String value() default 'ok' }
@Flag
final class Work {
  def <T> T identity(T value) { value }
  def run() {
    def callback = { String name = 'default', int count = 2 -> name * count }
    for (String name : ['a']) { println name }
    synchronized(this) { println (String) 'ok' }
    try { run() } catch (Exception) { println 'failed' }
  }
}

==================
Annotated implicit-return methods, modifier-only fields, diamond types and lambdas
==================
class Features {
    final static CMP = { a, b -> a <=> b }
    @Unroll 'implicit return feature'() {
        def values = new ArrayList<>()
        values.map(x -> helper(x))
        values.map((String x) -> { helper(x) })
    }
    public run() { helper(1) }
    def helper(x) { x }
}
